The Hebrew here is ha-satan, "the Accuser", a title with the article rather than a personal name. Many Christians identify him with Satan, the devil, while many Jewish readers and scholars see an officer of God's court; the notes on chapter 1 give the views.
In 33:4 Elihu says "God's spirit made me". Many Christians read this as the Holy Spirit, while Jewish readers take it as God's own breath or power; the verse itself does not use that name.
